reuse.why: Most sites go through the existing getScheduledAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold, but schedule-template.ts calls the split range/approx helpers with its own op dispatch instead of the shared getScheduledAmount.

duplication.why: The isbetween/isapprox/plain dispatch now exists twice: inside getScheduledAmount and again inline in schedule-template.ts.

placement.why: The rule helpers sit in shared/schedules.ts and the API type in api-models.ts, as the tree does, but one consumer keeps rule dispatch in the budget layer.

scope.why: Focused on the requested steps, though it leaves stale 'rounded midpoint' and 'furthest from zero' comments and contradictory release notes behind.

maintainability.why: The optional op parameter is passed at some sites and silently omitted at others (the preview in shared/schedules.ts, Balance.tsx), so approximate amounts get different answers by path, and the dispatch is duplicated in the template.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList dispatches on amountCondition.op itself instead of calling getScheduledAmount(value, false, op).

disguised_duplication.where: schedule-template.ts repeats getScheduledAmount's op dispatch, reshaped as a nested ternary over the split getRangedAmountWorstCase/getApproxAmountWorstCase helpers.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gained an optional op parameter; schedule-template.ts bypasses it with its own dispatch; computeSchedulePreviewTransactions (shared/schedules.ts) and Balance.tsx still call it without op, so the approximate rule is not applied there.
